ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, partners, UBOs, authorized signatories and general partners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Luxembourg FIU/CSSF warnings. PEP determination and enhanced due diligence apply under AML/CFT Law Article 2. All natural persons holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the partnership must be identified. Ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds verification are required for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced compliance classification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu and state formality portal https://www.guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script. Acceptable names may be in Luxembourgish, French or German, with official transliteration to the Latin alphabet for names originating in other scripts. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must include or be followed by the legal form suffix 'SCSp' or 'S.C.Sp.' for a Société en Commandite Spéciale. Names that conflict with an existing RCS registration or common-law trademarks are rejected. Use of the word 'Luxembourg' requires caution and may trigger additional administrative checks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection, the prospective incorporator may first submit a written request for reconsideration to the RCS registrar within 15 calendar days. If reconsideration is refused, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification; the appeal must be filed by licensed counsel, set out the grounds of violation of law, and name the Grand Ducal Ministry of Justice or RCS as responding party. Pending appeal, the proposed name remains blocked from parallel filings. Alternative resolution includes filing a new name application or seeking judicial review before the competent civil court in Luxembourg City.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional acceptance. A virtual office or pure mailbox is not enough for an SCSp under Luxembourg law. A Luxembourg-registered domiciliation agent may provide the legal seat, but the SCSp must maintain a genuine registered office at an approved address in Luxembourg, retain a Luxembourg-resident general partner or authorized corporate service provider, keep statutory books and records in Luxembourg, and have a physical location capable of receiving official correspondence and inspection. For a VPN and privacy SaaS business, remote operations are acceptable provided central administration supports Luxembourg substance and is not merely nominal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10% unannounced on-site inspection risk in the first year for an SCSp using a reputable Luxembourg law-firm or approved domiciliation agent. If the registered office is purely a virtual mailbox without demonstrable substance, the probability of inspection rises to approximately 25-30%, particularly when the business is engaged in network security or digital services that attract tax-authority scrutiny.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including the special limited partnership provisions introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; applicable sections include Articles 184-1 et seq. and the general provisions on partnerships, together with implementing regulations of the Registre de commerce et des sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS), 2, boulevard de la Foire, L-1528 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société / Acte constitutif (Limited Partnership Agreement) and the Statement of Registration (Déclaration de constitution) filed electronically through the LBR e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp. Contributions are freely agreed in the limited partnership agreement in cash, in kind, or as services. If cash contributions are made, they must be deposited in a blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution and can be released only after RCS registration; a banker's certificate evidencing the deposit must be available for the RCS file.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the limited partnership agreement and all subscription documents be approved, and the subscription to partnership interests by the initial limited partners be accepted on the terms set out in the partnership deed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Société en Commandite Spéciale be established at 12, rue de l'Industrie, L-4560 Differdange, Luxembourg, and may be relocated within the Grand Duchy by the general partner. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner be appointed as manager and authorized representative, empowered to sign RCS filings, open corporate bank accounts, and execute all regulatory formalities. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability check and constitutional pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - online name search portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the Luxembourg trade and companies register to confirm the proposed corporate name is available and does not infringe existing registrations or protected designations. Reserve a distinctive name for the SCSp, e.g. 'Lux Digital Privacy SCSp', and record the availability search report for the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport of each proposed partner
Certificate of legal existence and good standing of any corporate general partner
Power of attorney to local counsel or Luxembourg law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, amend the name and submit up to three alternatives; the rejection may be contested by representation to LBR if the conflicting mark is dormant or not protected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office (voluntary for private deed) and all partners; no government approval at drafting stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915. The deed must specify the corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate object covering the development and sale of VPN network privacy software, duration, contribution commitments, classes of partnership interests, powers of the general partner, distribution waterfall, and amendment procedure. Execute the deed by the general partner and all initial limited partners, either by private signature or before a Luxembourg notary, and date it.
required_dossiers: Articles/partnership deed of any corporate general partner
Consent of domiciliation agent if registered office is provided by an approved domiciliation company
Proof of identity of the beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or the RCS reviewer determines that a clause is illegal, execute an amending deed before the same notary; if a beneficial owner flag is raised, provide full source-of-funds documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked bank account and contribution deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (private sector) - no government authority involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the not-yet-registered SCSp at a licensed Luxembourg bank. Deposit the agreed initial cash contribution, which is determined contractually because the law imposes no minimum. Obtain a banker's certificate confirming that the funds are blocked until the RCS delivers the registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays opening due to KYC/AML requirements, supplement documentation promptly and escalate to the bank's legal department; alternative approved banks may be used, but the bank account must be in Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration application online at www.lbr.lu using the authenticated electronic signature of the general partner or a notary on behalf of the SCSp. Attach the executed partnership agreement, statement by the general partner, bank certificate if contributions were deposited, registered office lease or domiciliation contract, beneficial ownership register filing, and the RCS model statement. Submit the fee schedule, verify the draft extract, and await issuance of the registration number and corporate identification number.
required_dossiers: Statement of acceptance and consent of general partner
Bank certificate / blocked account confirmation (if cash contribution)
Registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
Criminal record extract for individual general partner or good-standing certificate for corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a deficiency notice, correct and re-submit through the same e-filing portal within 15 days; material deficiencies may require a notarized rectification instrument. If registration is refused, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and legal effectiveness of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) - official electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registrant's details are automatically published in the RESA gazette. Verify that the publication includes the exact name, registered office, legal form SCSp, general partner identity, and object. Download and archive the published extract as proof of third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: Copy of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette entry contains an error, file a correction request through LBR and obtain a rectified RESA notice; publication is deemed accurate from the date of RESA issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security, and data protection registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of RCS registration, notify the ACD of the SCSp's creation and request a Luxembourg tax identification number for income tax and municipal business tax. Submit a VAT registration form to the AED and, if annual taxable supplies exceed EUR 35,000, register for VAT; for the VPN/privacy product, also file a CNPD notification if processing personal data and, where applicable, appoint a data protection representative or DPO.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or CNPD registration applications are queried, respond through the respective electronic portals within the statutory 15-day to one-month cure periods; adverse decisions can be appealed to the Director of the ACD or the Administrative Tribunal within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Industry and Digital Technologies; no industrial establishment license is triggered by a software-only VPN SaaS activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating permit required for the VPN network privacy software activity; no manufacturing, production, or physical processing authorization is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA report or registration required for office-based software development and SaaS services under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge thresholds apply; adherence to Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE) for ICT equipment disposal, Directive 94/62/EC for packaging waste, and EU Ecodesign Regulation (EU) 2023/826 for servers is expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the competent commune or the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office; structural load inspection for server racks if the floor load exceeds 150 kg/m2; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering emergency exits, electrical installation, and ergonomic workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes and corporate income tax: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD, Luxembourg Inland Revenue). VAT and excise duties: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT, Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration). Unified digital portal: secured Business eSpace via MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate and file the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a civil-law notary or online RCS e-filing; the RCS registration automatically issues the national identification number (matricule) of Luxembourg format. Step 2: Submit the statutory commencement-of-activity declaration to the AEDT through the Business eSpace; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU followed by 8 digits). Step 3: As a fiscally transparent special limited partnership, the SCSp files an annual partner income-allocations declaration with the ACD; the SCSp itself is not registered for corporate income tax or net wealth tax. Step 4: Non-resident corporate partners do not need a separate Luxembourg TIN unless the SCSp's local operations create a deemed permanent establishment, in which case the partner registers with the ACD competent regional tax office. Step 5: For B2C electronically supplied VPN services to EU consumers, the SCSp registers for the OSS Union scheme on the AEDT/VD online portal. A foreign supplier without a Luxembourg establishment must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative unless reverse charge or the OSS scheme applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory design and lacks legal personality under the law of 12 July 2013. It is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax; profits are attributed directly and pro rata to the general and limited partners. Non-resident corporate partners are taxable in Luxembourg only on income attributable to a deemed permanent establishment arising from the SCSp's VPN SaaS activity conducted from Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Relevant statutorily available elections: (i) irrevocable election for full tax transparency under Article 14/4 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LITL) for commercial partnerships, although the SCSp is already transparent by default; (ii) VAT group election as a single taxable person (assujetti unique) under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (iii) waiver of the EUR 35,000 small-business VAT exemption upon exceeding the threshold; (iv) OSS Union scheme election for cross-border B2C supplies of VPN and digital services; (v) BEPS/ATAD II hybrid-mismatch election and declaration via Form 103 to the ACD where dual classification of the SCSp is identified.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (VAT) implemented under Council Directive 2006/112/EC and the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established taxable persons under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 in a 12-month period, mandatory VAT registration and invoicing apply. Non-established suppliers have no registration threshold. Electronically supplied VPN/digital services to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's member state from the first transaction irrespective of turnover, so OSS registration is required without any threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls or mandatory digital stamping for domestic B2B supplies. E-invoicing is interoperable under PEPPOL/EN 16931 standards and mandatory for B2G invoices submitted through the national e-space procurement portal. Cross-border intra-EU B2B e-invoicing and transaction-based reporting are not yet mandatory; they become effective from 1 July 2030 under the VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VPN network and privacy software constitute electronically supplied services under Article 58 of Directive 2006/112/EC. Supplies to non-EU B2B customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT where the customer is established outside the EU; supplies to non-EU B2C consumers are zero-rated with the place of supply determined by the consumer's usual residence evidenced through IP geolocation, billing address and payment gateway data. Physical goods exports are zero-rated provided the goods depart EU customs territory within the legal timeframe. EU-destination supplies follow normal rules: B2B supplies are subject to reverse charge in the customer's member state; B2C supplies are declared through the Luxembourg OSS scheme in the destination member state.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg export declaration (Single Administrative Document) and Movement Reference Number registered in the EU Export Control System (ECS/ICS2)
Commercial invoice and executed contract identifying the non-EU customer and the exact nature of the VPN/digital service or goods
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of goods from EU customs territory
Bank transfer receipt, Stripe or Paymentwall payout statement evidencing receipt of consideration
IP geolocation logs, device records and subscriber registration data evidencing non-EU place of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD may audit export zero-rating and place-of-supply claims within a five-year assessment period, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or false declarations. Unsubstantiated or fictitious export exemptions trigger retrospective VAT assessment at the 17% standard rate, statutory default interest of 0.8% per month, and administrative fines of 10% to 50% of the tax at stake depending on intent. Criminal sanctions for documentary VAT fraud include fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment from eight days to five years. The SCSp's general partner bears joint and several civil liability for the partnership's VAT debts. Luxembourg imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline due to free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU; the 180-day parameter reflects the international trade-finance and AML/CTF benchmark applied by Luxembourg credit institutions to SaaS export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and Luxembourg's representative in the Eurosystem. Banking and e-money supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no separate Foreign Exchange Administration; currency matters are governed by the EU liberalisation rules (TFEU Articles 63-66).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted: there is no FX licensing, no exchange-control approval, no investment-screening or profit-repatriation permit regime. An SCSp is a tax-transparent contractual partnership without separate legal personality; profit distributions to non-resident limited partners are generally exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax when the entity remains fiscally transparent and adequate substance is evidenced. Remittance friction is limited to bank-level AML/KYC source-of-funds confirmation, CRS/FATCA classification and UBO transparency. No convertibility hurdles apply to EUR/USD, EUR/GBP or EUR/CHF flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, no mandatory conversion and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds or any other foreign-currency receipts. Export collections may be retained indefinitely in designated foreign-currency accounts. Compliance is limited to ECB/BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting: the servicing bank applies the ECB classification codes to each cross-border flow, and corporates maintain the supporting invoices and contracts for audit. No proportional conversion ratio is prescribed for EUR-denominated or multi-currency holding.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High (restricted). European-authorised e-money and payment institutions such as Payoneer Europe, Wise Europe, Revolut and Wallter are viable for settlement sub-accounts and for aggregating Stripe and Paymentwall proceeds, but they are not a substitute for a primary Luxembourg bank account. They are legally constrained by EEA passporting under PSD2 and MiCA, impose materially lower transaction caps, require narrow CDD acceptance for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced VPN/network-privacy profile, and create monthly reconciliation friction. Offshore non-EEA, unlicensed or MSB-type digital EMIs are not viable for a Luxembourg-compliant treasury and will be rejected by CSSF-regulated banks as sub-account counterparties; they may be used only as light collection gateways subject to full OFAC/EU sanctions screening and an immediate onward sweep to BCEE, BIL or BGL BNP Paribas. Recommended treasury pattern: Stripe and Paymentwall as acquiring gateways; Payoneer or Wise Business as an EEA-licensed collection and settlement EMI; and BIL or BCEE as bank of record for capital, tax, hedging and disbursement flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in substance: Luxembourg risk committees systematically require a face-to-face interview, either on-site or through a CSSF-compliant verified video process, for at least one natural person holding a mandate. That person is normally the SCSp general partner, a limited partner owning 25% or more, or a formally appointed authorised signatory. Pure remote opening is granted only to applicants with an existing private-banking relationship or on fintech-friendly platforms using qualified electronic signatures; for a newly formed SCSp with a non-resident general partner and a VPN/network-security scope, an in-person KYC session at the Luxembourg head office is the effective norm. The interview covers economic substance, expected payment flows, beneficial ownership of the partnership, product compliance and the destination of outbound disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN and network-privacy SaaS flagged by the underwriting department as an anonymity-enhancing technology and therefore a medium-to-high money-laundering and dual-use cyber concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the product AML/CTF risk assessment; (ii) a written explanation of the VPN logging and encryption architecture; (iii) the customer identity-verification and age-gating policy; (iv) ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 Type II attestations; (v) a third-party penetration test report dated within 180 days; (vi) the acceptable-use policy with expressly prohibited criminal activities; (vii) OFAC/EU restrictive-measures and sanctions-screening procedures; (viii) alignment statements with the EU Digital Services Act and Luxembourg data-protection law; (ix) a customer abuse-reporting and takedown SOP; and (x) a board-adopted AML/KYC policy corresponding to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced rating.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp partnership form with a non-public register of partners and broad non-resident ownership, creating uncertainty as to the identification of ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) the executed partnership agreement; (ii) a fresh RCS excerpt of the SCSp issued within 30 days; (iii) the register of partners, encrypted for confidentiality; (iv) the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners confirmation and supporting declaration; (v) an organisational chart showing percentage interests; (vi) passport identification and proof of address of the general partner and each partner holding 25% or more; (vii) tax-residency certificates of all partners; (viii) a general-partner resolution approving the bank mandate; and (ix) a capital-flow narrative showing the commercial origin and economic substance of each contribution to satisfy the source-of-wealth test.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border collection from Stripe and Paymentwall spanning customer geographies that include high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions and triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) the merchant agreements with Stripe and Paymentwall including their PSD2 licensing details; (ii) the transaction-monitoring policy with thresholds and alert-rule matrix; (iii) the country block-list and risk-based scoring procedure; (iv) sample KYB/KYC onboarding files of the first twenty enterprise customers; (v) a 90-day historical cash-flow and device-telemetry report reconciled to the accounting ledgers; (vi) a volume-cap projection for jurisdictions categorised as high-risk; and (vii) evidence of a controlled payment-flow map rather than a rent-a-license or pass-through arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital contribution from a non-resident partner with no prior Luxembourg banking history and suspicion of conduit, loan-back or shell financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) the executed capital contribution undertaking and call notice; (ii) the SCSp general-partner resolution authorising the call; (iii) a source-of-funds package comprising three months of bank statements, tax returns or exit documentation; (iv) a bank reference letter from a regulated source institution; (v) an intragroup and ownership chart demonstrating commercial rationale; and (vi) a signed statement confirming that no back-to-back financing or revolving credit facilities are used by the partners. The bank will then admit the contribution under escalated due diligence and the BCL statistical purpose classification of direct investment equity capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner subscriptions enter Luxembourg via SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp account at a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank, with the SCSp represented by its general partner. The remittance instruction must identify the underlying partner, the economic purpose and the ECB/BCL balance-of-payments classification: equity contributions are coded as direct investment equity capital using BoP matrix codes 511 or 512, and must not be coded as general services or software licensing. The receiving bank executes sanctions and OFAC/EU screening, source-of-funds enhanced due diligence, CRS/FATCA classification and BCL external statistics registration. Contributions above EUR 100,000 are prepared for treasury or risk-committee approval with the signed subscription deed, general-partner resolution, updated register of partners, UBO declaration and RBE filing. EU-based partners may settle in euro via SEPA Credit Transfer or T2 for high-value same-day finality; cross-currency injections flow through the bank's correspondent network, with US-dollar transfers using SWIFT, CHIPS or Fedwire, and are converted at arm's length euro reference rates. No foreign-investment approval is required, as Luxembourg operates full capital-account liberalisation under TFEU Article 63.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments run over multiple rails: EUR disbursements within the EEA use SEPA Credit Transfer; high-value and urgent euro payments of EUR 1 million or above settle via T2 or TARGET2; USD, GBP and CHF disbursements are executed by SWIFT MT103 through the bank's correspondent accounts using CHIPS and Fedwire in the United States and CHAPS and FPS in the United Kingdom, accompanied by full legal names, sanctions pre-screening and valid BoP purpose codes such as other business services or computer and information services. Hardware procurement and co-location capacity purchases are supported by irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP600 and documentary collections under URC522 arranged through the trade desks of BGL BNP Paribas or Société Générale Luxembourg. Treasury sweeps between the Luxembourg bank account and EEA-licensed EMI sub-accounts use SEPA Instant Credit Transfer. Every disbursement in a non-euro currency is covered either by an existing forward contract or converted on the payment date; no export-surrender permit is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable plain-vanilla foreign-exchange forwards executed with an EEA-licensed bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a reduced foreign-exchange single-transaction confirmation.
Cross-currency swaps, mark-to-market and collateralised under standard Credit Support Annexes, for long-term USD and GBP revenue and cost conversion.
FX swaps and plain spot FX operations for working-capital conversion.
Zero-cost collars and structured forwards accepted only when the underlying exposure is fully business-linked and the product passes the CSSF suitability and CRD governance tests.
Non-deliverable forwards limited to currencies with non-deliverable regimes such as TRY and RUB, booked only with EEA credit institutions and subject to EMIR and CSDR margin rules.
Foreign-exchange options designated as hedges under IFRS 9 cash-flow hedging, with hedge documentation, ratio testing and rebalancing provisions issued at inception.

Natural hedging through euro and US-dollar money-market positions and currency-synchronised receivables and payables. Crypto-asset, digital-asset or synthetic-currency linked hedging instruments are expressly non-permissible for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced treasury profile.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation and RBE update declaration (Register of Beneficial Owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); Ministry of Justice administrative control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On any transfer of partnership interests: within one month after the transfer. When no ownership change occurs, the general partner and registered agent execute an annual no-change confirmation by 31 January of each following calendar year; the certificate is retained at the registered office (no mandatory nil RBE filing where no change exists).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file RBE updates within one month: administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 and criminal fine up to EUR 5,000; repeated violations can be published and may lead to RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and statutory audit report (deposit with RCS if audit is mandatory or audit was specifically resolved; otherwise the SCSp’s accounts are exclusively internal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Central Balance Sheet Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end; where the financial year closes on 31 December, filing deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory injunction and coercive daily financial penalties (astreinte), administrative fines up to EUR 4,000, and possible judicial dissolution after persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registered-agent register-audit certificate (maintenance of statutory registers, minutes, partnership registers and registered-office file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing — certificate is delivered to the general partner and kept at the registered office, available for inspection by Luxembourg Business Registers, tax authorities and auditors.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 30 June following the calendar year-end; statutory-register updates are recorded at transfer or appointment date and RCS data is updated within one month of any registered information change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing statutory registers may make the general partner jointly and severally liable for damages; administrative fines of up to EUR 4,000 may be imposed following inspection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Luxembourg law (law of 19 December 2002 as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU), a statutory audit is required if two of the three following criteria are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. An SCSp without legal personality is not automatically subject to published statutory audit; audit becomes compulsory if the partnership agreement so provides, if it is used as a regulated fund vehicle (CSSF/RAIF), or if the general partner is required by group law to consolidate the SCSp.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) under the modified law of 19 December 2002 and CSSF accounting circulars; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for consolidated accounts or by election.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year, by 31 January, the general partner issues a confirmation request to all general and limited partners identifying current beneficial owners. Partners respond in writing or via e-signature. The registered agent reconciles the responses against the RBE registration. If any direct or indirect ownership change has occurred, an RBE update is filed within one month from the date of the transfer. If no change, the signed no-change confirmation is filed in the statutory registers as the annual UBO confirmation record. A written record of each annual confirmation must be kept at the registered office for at least five years for AML/KYC purposes.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 15,000 (if mandatory/opted-in; no statutory audit fee applies to a below-threshold SCSp unless contractually agreed)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: SCSp is fiscally transparent: 0% Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT) at the partnership level. A fully taxable Luxembourg company is subject to an aggregate Luxembourg City headline rate of 24.94% (17% CIT + 1.19% unemployment-solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax). Each partner is taxed directly on his allocated share under his own residence regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax on the transparent SCSp. Downstream incentives passed through to taxable partners: 80% IP-Box exemption for qualifying VPN software/IP income, 20% incremental R&D tax credit, the participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gain income, and treaty/credit relief in the partner's residence state.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiration). Losses are allocated to partners and carried forward at partner level; annual utilization is capped at EUR 17,500,000 plus 50% of the taxable base exceeding EUR 17,500,000.
